findings.title: Customer requests pilot expansion of training benefit to Clinical Ops group
findings.description: Simone wants to pilot the training benefit with ~40 study coordinators out of a ~140-person clinical operations group, citing high turnover and wanting a retention 'delta' to justify spend to her VP. This is a request to expand the services/benefit footprint to a new employee group, not a defect in or missing capability of the BetterBark product itself. A working session to design the pilot was agreed for the following week.
findings.quote: I want to talk about extending the training benefit to our clinical operations group
findings.severity_reason: Business/services expansion request with no product defect or missing capability involved.
findings.match_note: Not a product bug or feature gap; it's a services rollout ask, so it doesn't correspond to any catalogue issue.

findings.title: Customer questions unexplained org-wide dip in May engagement report
findings.description: Simone's monthly engagement report showed an org-wide dip in May that didn't match her anecdotal sense of activity, with numbers rebounding the following month. She suspects it could be a reporting artifact rather than a real behavior change and wants it confirmed before presenting to her VP in mid-July. No specific defect, data field, or repro is identified yet; Maya committed to pull the underlying May session data and report back rather than a conclusion being reached on the call.
findings.quote: my monthly engagement report showed a dip in May that didn't match what I was seeing anecdotally
findings.severity_reason: No confirmed defect stated; request is for an internal data investigation, not a specific reproducible product problem.
findings.match_note: Too vague to be an engineering-actionable finding as of end of call; not resolved as either real or artifact, and no repro/location given.

findings.title: Password-reset emails delayed up to ~30 minutes, worse during morning peak login
findings.description: Password-reset emails for the training platform take a long time to arrive, sometimes intermittently; one coordinator timed a delay of roughly 25-30 minutes before the email showed up, by which point she had already emailed Simone's team and no longer needed it. Simone reports the delays cluster during the morning login rush (e.g., around 9am when the whole office logs in) and are less frequent later in the day. The customer confirmed the email was not caught in spam/quarantine — it arrived in the regular inbox but with a send timestamp 20+ minutes after the request, indicating the delay is upstream (generation/dispatch), not a mail-filter issue. Foxglove does not use SSO for this app (IT declined to federate it), so the password-reset flow is members' primary login recovery path, making this delay more impactful for them than for SSO accounts.
findings.quote: The reset email takes forever to arrive. Sometimes. That's the maddening part — it's not always.
findings.severity_reason: Real, confirmed delay (not a filter/quarantine issue) that drives support volume and blocks self-service login recovery for up to ~30 minutes during peak times, but users eventually receive the email and can log in; no permanent lockout.
findings.match_note: Same symptom (reset emails delayed, worse at peak/morning hours) and same underlying scope (queueing behind bulk sends at peak) as PROJ-142; add Foxglove Pharma as an affected account.

findings.title: Foxglove does not use SSO for the training platform (IT declined to federate)
findings.description: Simone explained that Foxglove's IT team declined to federate the training platform via SSO, so members log in with email/password directly instead. This is a customer-side configuration/policy decision, not a BetterBark product defect or missing capability (SSO itself is already supported, as used by other accounts). It was parked as a future topic for Simone to raise internally with her IT security lead, who has reportedly warmed to federating more apps.
findings.quote: our IT wouldn't federate a non-critical app, so our people log in with email and password directly
findings.severity_reason: Not a product issue; it's a customer-side IT policy choice that could change independently of any product action.
findings.match_note: No catalogue match; SSO capability already exists in the product (cf. PROJ-064 involves an SSO account), so this is a customer adoption decision, not a gap.

findings.title: Customer asks for interim messaging to reduce panic re-requests during reset delay
findings.description: Simone asked what she could tell her team in the meantime so they stop panic-emailing support while waiting on delayed reset emails. Maya suggested interim guidance: request once and wait a few minutes rather than clicking repeatedly, since multiple requests can invalidate earlier tokens and add confusion. This is a stopgap tied directly to the password-reset delay issue already raised, not a separate product problem.
findings.quote: is there anything I can tell my people so they don't panic-email us? Even just "it can take a while during busy periods, don't request it twice"
findings.severity_reason: Interim communication workaround for an already-captured issue, not a distinct product defect.
findings.match_note: Directly tied to the reset-email delay finding (line 32 / PROJ-142); filed as a workaround request, not a separate issue.
